title: {{NAME}} and the Time-Bot Who Met a T-Rex
moral: Curiosity is how we make the impossible happen.
character_anchor: Bright children's book cartoon illustration, bold outlines, vivid flat colours. {{NAME}}, a young boy with brown hair and blue eyes, wearing a red and chrome-striped jacket, black cargo trousers, and silver-toed boots — same child, same face, same exact outfit in every image.

pages.content:
{{NAME}} had built TEMPO with one specific purpose: time observation.

Not time travel, which was too complicated and also probably illegal. Just observation: a small probe that could slip through a temporal fold, take readings, and come back.

The first test, a quick jump to a Tuesday two weeks prior, worked perfectly.

The second test, aimed at 65 million years ago, also worked perfectly.

TEMPO returned with data, a claw mark across its hull, and a thin layer of prehistoric mud.

"Excellent," said {{NAME}}. Then he looked at the claw mark more carefully.

No text, no words, no letters anywhere in the image.

pages.content:
He reviewed TEMPO's visual data on his tablet.

A Cretaceous forest. Enormous tree ferns. The probe descending into a clearing.

Then: the head of a Tyrannosaurus Rex, very close, examining the probe with one enormous amber eye. The T-Rex had patted the probe once, hence the claw mark. Then it had stepped back and watched it with what could only be described as curiosity.

{{NAME}} rewound the video. Watched the T-Rex's eye again.

"You weren't attacking it," he said aloud. "You were investigating it."

No text, no words, no letters anywhere in the image.

pages.content:
He modified TEMPO with a speaker and sent it back.

This time he watched in real-time: the probe descending into the same clearing. The T-Rex appearing at the treeline, already alert, recognising the shape.

{{NAME}} sent a sound through TEMPO's speaker: three short tones, low and clear.

The T-Rex tilted its enormous head.

{{NAME}} sent the tones again.

The T-Rex replied with a low rumble that shook the probe's sensors.

TEMPO translated it as: acknowledged.

Dynamic shot of the small silver robot TEMPO hovering in a prehistoric clearing, the enormous head of a Tyrannosaurus Rex lowered toward it, both seemingly in conversation, ancient trees and ferns framing the extraordinary scene. No text, no words, no letters anywhere in the image.

pages.content:
They communicated for six minutes before {{NAME}} had to return TEMPO.

In those six minutes he learned: the T-Rex had seen three different temporal probes over its lifetime. It had investigated them all. It found them interesting but not dangerous.

It lived alone. It was approximately forty years old. It had explored most of its territory and found it sufficient.

Then it sent one more sound before TEMPO left. TEMPO's translation program took a moment, then offered: come again.

{{NAME}} sat back in his chair and stared at the ceiling.

pages.content:
He sat at the edge of his bed that night, reading back through the translation logs.

A forty-year-old T-Rex. Had seen three probes. Remembered them all. Was curious enough to say: come again.

{{NAME}} looked out at the night sky, thinking about how the universe was always larger than whatever box you tried to put it in.

He turned off his lamp and lay in the dark.

On his desk, TEMPO's status light blinked slowly, green, patient, ready.

Somewhere across sixty-five million years, an enormous amber eye blinked in the dark of an ancient forest, and waited.
